## Face form of the gravity work (`gravity-work: face`, `face-wallc`) {#sec-ch06-face}

The face form books, in cell $i$, the work the scheme's own $x_1$ mass fluxes do against gravity: each face's
flux carries mass from the face potential to the cell's centroid potential. Its derivation is the template of
@eq-ch06-dwork-booked with $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$, written out as @eq-ch06-dwork-face in @sec-ch06-dwork. This section
covers what the code does around it: it replaces the cell work the forcing added, it adds the curvature flux for
the high-order reconstructions, it keeps the cell work in the wall cells under `face-wallc`, and it needs the
implicit operator to carry it when an implicit scheme is on.

Local symbols: $m_i=\rho_iv_{1,i}$ is the $x_1$ mass flux density at cell $i$ (code `rhov`); $\mathcal K$ is the
curvature flux of NOTATION section 3. Tracked in ISSUES.md.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Book the $x_1$ gravity work as the flux difference of potential energy across a cell's faces,
@eq-ch06-dwork-face, so that, with the corrected-PE work off, $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ is conserved exactly.

**Data.** Reads the total $x_1$ mass flux $F$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$] on the two faces of each cell (dry row plus the
mass-carrying species rows), the face and centroid potentials, and with $\mathcal K$ the $m$ of three cells; writes
the energy-row correction [W m$^{-3}$] of the interior cells.

**Placement.** Each stage, after the $x_1$ flux is final (positivity limiter and sedimentation) and after the
forcings; before the implicit solve when one runs with `face`, after it with `face-wallc`.

**Activation.** `gravity-work: face`, the default (`gravity_work`,
{{< code src/forcing/const_gravity.cpp ConstGravityOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), or `face-wallc`, which keeps the cell
work in the two $x_1$ wall cells. Turns off the gravity-work fixer; the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is on
with it by default.

**Guarantee / limits.** On a closed column: plain `face` with `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` keeps
$E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exact; default `face`, with the corrected-PE work on, keeps $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+P$
exact instead (@sec-ch06-dwork); `face-wallc` has no exact invariant, because of its two wall cells. Second order,
fourth in the interior with the cp3/cp5/weno5 curvature flux, first in the wall cells.

**Evidence.** `cellface_check.py` `[C1]`, `[C3]`-`[C5]`; `test_forcing` curvature case, read from the source, not
run here.
:::

With `gravity-work: face` the corrected-PE work of @sec-ch06-dwork is on by default
(`SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT`); this section describes the face form with that switch off, which is how the
plain face-form tests run. The curvature flux is "$\mathcal K$" in the derivation note.[^ch06-face-src]

[^ch06-face-src]: The face form and the fixer came in with chengcli/snapy#283.

### Derivation

The stage adds the cell work $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ through the forcing (@sec-ch06-cell). The face form replaces it:
the energy row receives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta E_i &\leftarrow \Delta E_i + \Delta t\,\big(W^{\mathrm{face}}_i - W^{\mathrm{cell}}_i - \nabla_{\!1}\!\cdot g_1\mathcal K\big),\\
\mathcal K_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac{1}{12}(x_{1,i}-x_{1,i-1})(m_i-m_{i-1}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-face-energy}

with $\mathcal K=0$ on every physical $x_1$ face and only for cp3, cp5 and weno5 reconstructions in $x_1$.
@eq-ch06-face-energy is booked as `gravity_energy_correction`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}),
with the curvature term from `curv_flux1`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

The face form conserves $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ exactly on a closed column (`cellface_check.py` `[C1]`, to
$3.9\times10^{-15}$ relative on Cartesian and spherical-polar columns). $\mathcal K$ does not change that: it is a
flux, zero at both walls, so its divergence sums to zero (`[C4]`, $5\times10^{-17}$). Its purpose is accuracy. A
high-order reconstruction's face flux exceeds the point value $m$ by $\tfrac{h^2}{12}(\partial_1^2m+\dots)$, and the
face form books that excess as work; $\nabla_{\!1}\!\cdot g_1\mathcal K$ removes the $\partial_1^2m$ part. Against
the exact cell average of $g_1m$ and with exact point fluxes, the face form is second order in interior and wall
cells, and the face form with $\mathcal K$ is fourth order in the interior and first order in the two wall cells,
where $\mathcal K$ is present on one face only (`[C3]`, `[C4]`; orders 2.00 and 2.00, then 3.99 and 1.00, at
$n_1$ = 128 to 256). `face-wallc` books $W^{\mathrm{cell}}$ in the two wall cells, so its defect is
exactly their cell-minus-face work (`[C5]`). Provenance of every `[Cn]` as in @sec-ch06-cell.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch06-face-stencil shows what the face form reads: the two $x_1$ face fluxes of cell $i$ after the positivity
limiter and sedimentation, the face and centroid potentials, and, with $\mathcal K$, $m$ in cells $i-1$, $i$ and
$i+1$. The fluxes are the total mass flux, the dry row plus every mass-carrying species row. Physical $x_1$ faces
are the only ones where $\mathcal K$ is zeroed; seams between blocks keep it, reading the exchanged ghost. The
work is explicit and added once per stage. With an implicit scheme and `gravity-work: face` the correction is
added before the solve and the solve carries the face work in its energy row (@sec-ch06-vic); with `face-wallc`
it is swapped in after the solve. @fig-ch06-face-order shows the measured orders.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch06-face-stencil
#| fig-cap: "What the face form reads. (a) Cell i: the potential flux phi F at its two x1 faces (orange triangles) and the centroid potential phi_i (sky-blue dot), weighted by the distances from the centroid to each face. (b) The curvature flux K (bluish-green triangles) at the bottom wall: it is zero on the wall face (vermillion label), so wall cell 0 sees K on one face only; the ghost cell (hatched) is not read."
#| fig-alt: "Two panels: three cells with face markers and a centroid marker; and a wall with a hatched ghost cell, three interior cells and K markers on the two interior faces."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch06.fig_face_stencil import make_fig
make_fig()
```


### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| mass and potential fluxes | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `potential_flux1` | `gravity-work` |
| face work | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `face_gravity_work` | `gravity-work` |
| curvature flux | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `curv_flux1` | `reconstruct` |
| face minus cell, wall cells | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `gravity_energy_correction` | `face-wallc` |
| x1 wall test | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::is_x1_wall >}} | `is_x1_wall` | |
| implicit warning | {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}} | `face_work_in_operator` | `implicit-scheme` |

: Code map of the face form. {#tbl-ch06-face-code}

1. Sum the total $x_1$ mass flux over the dry and species rows as `vertical_mass_flux1`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
2. Form the face and cell potentials and the two divergences in `potential_flux_div`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. Book the face work as `face_gravity_work` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
4. Subtract the curvature flux for cp3, cp5 and weno5, zeroed at physical faces, as `curv_flux1`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
5. Replace the cell work, keeping it in the wall cells under `face-wallc`, as `gravity_energy_correction`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

A user can hit the setup warning "gravity-work: face-wallc with an implicit scheme: the face work sits outside the
implicit operator" (also for `face` with `implicit-scheme: 0`).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_forcing.release` | curvature excess removed | $10^{-9}$ abs. | test threshold |
| `test_forcing.release` | no horizontal mass divergence | $10^{-10}$ rel. | test threshold |
| `test_gravity_work_fixer_python` | face-wallc arm, reported | n/a | reported only |
| `test_implicit_face_work_operator_python` | rest column, Courant 66-657 | $10^{-11}$ | `EPE_TOL` |

: Tests of the face form; assertions read from the test sources at the pin, not run. {#tbl-ch06-face-tests}

`vertical_gravity_work_removes_the_curvature_excess` sets a quadratic $m$ on six cells. It requires the off-wall
excess to equal $\Delta t\,\tfrac{h^2}{12}\cdot2\cdot0.04\cdot0.03$ for cp3 and five-point reconstructions
and zero otherwise, to $10^{-9}$ absolute, as `expected` ({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp vertical_gravity_work_removes_the_curvature_excess >}}). The
plain face form is tested with `SNAP_GRAVITY_WORK_RADIAL_EXACT=0` set in the registration
(`set_tests_properties` in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). The curvature test also has a CUDA case.
Measured values at the pin are **missing evidence**.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
With an implicit scheme, the face work must be inside the implicit operator; `face-wallc` books it after the solve,
and a tall column then blows up at acoustic Courant about 66.[^ch06-face-283]
:::

[^ch06-face-283]: The tall-column blow-up is recorded in chengcli/snapy#283.

- The work is $O(h^2)$ in every cell without $\mathcal K$, and first order in the wall cells with it.
- `face-wallc` does not conserve $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ in its two wall cells (`[C5]`).
- The orders above use exact point fluxes; with the scheme's own fluxes the reconstruction and Riemann errors add.
- Combinations with the study switches: @sec-ch12-matrix.
